result.summary: 2024 was a busy year for Amodei's public timelines. Besides the eight claims already recorded (Ezra Klein in April, a June interview, SWE-bench in November), the October essay 'Machines of Loving Grace' says powerful AI could come 'as early as 2026' and could compress 50-100 years of biology into 5-10 years. In the 11 November Lex Fridman transcript he says that extrapolating the capability curves points to 'by 2026 or 2027'.

reply_text:
I found three new dated predictions from 2024, along with several near-misses and items I left out on purpose. Two are in Amodei's essay "Machines of Loving Grace" (October 2024) and one is in the Lex Fridman Podcast #452 transcript (11 November 2024). I didn't come across any of the eight claims you've already recorded, so none are marked as already_recorded.

**What I left out and why:**
- **Business forecasts.** On CNBC's Squawk Box (23 April 2024) he said training costs would grow from about $1 billion next year to $5–10 billion in 2025–2026. On Lex Fridman he forecast compute clusters, including clusters able to run "millions" of model copies within two to three years. Both are spending or compute plans, so they stay out.
- **Undated but close.** On CNBC he said models would "probably relatively soon" do many tasks better than humans. I didn't list it under undated because in the same interview he says AGI is not "a fully coherent concept". You may want to look at it yourself.

**Gaps in what I could read:**
- Only about the first 29,000 characters of the Lex Fridman transcript loaded. The line I quote is the episode's opening clip, and the same words are said again later in the "AGI" section, which I couldn't read. The SWE-bench claim you already have is also beyond what loaded.
- Only about the first 35,000 characters of the essay loaded, so its later sections weren't checked. The first time I tried to open the essay, the tool refused it.
- Two items in the JSON aren't from 2024. A LinkedIn post about the Logan Bartlett interview is dated about October 2023; Dwarkesh Patel and other interview results were from 2026. Both are noted under other_years.
- I used 8 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings, counting the refused one. The first fixed search ran once; my code broke while printing its results, but I read them from the saved output without searching again.
